prompt: Merchants capture customer emails for out-of-stock products, configure auto-send or approval mode from the admin, and view a log of all notifications sent.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchants capture customer emails for out-of-stock products, configure auto-send or approval mode from the admin, and view a log of all notifications sent.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version prevents duplicate signups from the same email for the same product, shows subscription counts per product in the admin, lets the merchant toggle auto-send without losing data, and logs every notification sent with timestamp and recipient count. Handle the edge case where a product restocks while a customer is signing up. Make the Notify Me button visually clear on product pages without disrupting the layout.

plan.dataFlow: A customer viewing an out-of-stock product submits their email via the storefront widget; the system records the subscription only if that email is not already subscribed for that product and the product is still out of stock at the moment of submission. When an inventory restocked event fires, the system looks up all pending subscriptions for the restocked product. In auto-send mode, notification emails are dispatched immediately and each subscription is marked notified; in approval mode, subscriptions are held in a pending-approval state until a merchant approves the batch from the admin panel. Every notification dispatch — whether auto or manual — creates a notification log entry recording the product, recipient count, and timestamp. The admin panel surfaces per-product subscription counts and the full notification log, and allows the merchant to toggle between auto-send and approval mode without affecting existing subscription records.

triggers.event: a product's inventory level is restored to a positive quantity
triggers.idempotency: if notifications for the same product restock event have already been dispatched or queued, treat subsequent deliveries of the same event as a no-op

capabilities.description: Verify whether the product variant is still out of stock at the moment of subscription submission.
Persist a customer's email subscription for a specific out-of-stock product variant.
Retrieve all active subscriptions for a product variant that has just restocked.
Retrieve product title and variant details to include in the notification email.
Determine whether the merchant's current configuration calls for auto-send or approval mode.
Deliver a restock notification email to each subscribed customer for the restocked product.
Update each subscription's status after a notification attempt is made or approved.
Create a log record capturing the product, recipient count, send mode, and timestamp for each dispatch event.
Fetch the full notification log for display in the admin panel.
Aggregate pending subscription counts per product variant for the admin dashboard.
Persist the merchant's chosen send mode (auto-send or approval) to the merchant configuration.
Mark a held batch of subscriptions as approved for dispatch in approval mode.

persistence.name: merchant_settings
persistence.purpose: Stores the merchant's global configuration for the app, including the active send mode.

columns.name: send_mode
columns.purpose: whether the merchant has chosen auto-send or approval mode

persistence.name: subscriptions
persistence.purpose: Records each customer email signup for a specific out-of-stock product variant, and tracks whether notification has been sent.

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the product the customer signed up for

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the specific variant the customer signed up for

columns.name: notification_log_id
columns.purpose: links to the notification log entry that covered this subscription

persistence.keyedBy: one row per unique combination of customer email and product variant

persistence.name: notification_logs
persistence.purpose: Records every notification dispatch event with its outcome, recipient count, and send mode used.

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the product for which notifications were sent

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the specific variant for which notifications were sent

persistence.keyedBy: one row per dispatch event per product variant

transitions.trigger: restock event received and merchant is in approval mode
restock event received and merchant is in auto-send mode and email delivered
merchant approves the batch and email is delivered
subscription found to be a duplicate or product was back in stock when the customer signed up
merchant explicitly discards the pending batch

invariants: exactly one subscription row exists per customer email and product variant combination
a subscription in notified or skipped state never transitions to any other state
a subscription may only move to awaiting-approval when the merchant's send mode is approval at the time of the restock event
every transition to notified must produce exactly one notification_logs entry referencing the batch

externalContracts.purpose: Accept a customer's email signup for an out-of-stock product variant from the storefront widget.
Retrieve the current merchant configuration including send mode.
Update the merchant's send mode preference.
Return per-product-variant subscription counts and the list of pending subscribers for the admin dashboard.
Return the full paginated notification log for display in the admin panel.
Approve a held batch of restock notifications for a product variant in approval mode.
Discard a held batch of restock notifications, marking those subscriptions as skipped.

edgeCases: A customer submits their email for a product that restocked between the page load and form submission — the system must verify stock at submission time and reject the signup with a clear message that the item is now available.
The same customer email is submitted twice for the same product variant — the second submission must be silently deduplicated with a success response to prevent enumeration of existing subscribers.
The restock event is delivered more than once for the same product variant — if notifications are already dispatched or queued for that variant, subsequent event deliveries must be treated as no-ops.

The merchant switches from approval mode to auto-send while a batch is in awaiting-approval state — those subscriptions remain in awaiting-approval and must be explicitly approved or discarded; the mode change does not retroactively dispatch them.

One or more email addresses in a batch are undeliverable — the system must record the failure per subscription and still mark the remaining recipients as notified, ensuring the log entry reflects the actual dispatched count.

A product variant restocks and then immediately goes out of stock again before the approval is granted — the merchant should see a warning in the admin that the variant is no longer in stock before confirming the dispatch.
